clue.text: Service providing overhead savings for those in deep water

definitions.text: Service providing overhead savings for those in deep water

parts.words: Service providing overhead savings for those in deep water
parts.note: overhead savings sounds like money kept down on running costs, but here it means rescues carried out from above by helicopter for people struggling at sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhead savings' tempts a business reading about cutting costs; the savings are lives saved by aircraft flying overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: The coastguard helicopter service lifts people from the sea, saving them from above.

clue.text: Leave an orchestra while it's playing

parts.note: the indefinite article an can be shortened to a
an orchestra is a musical band
a show that is playing is said to be on

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of a concert while the orchestra is still performing.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something or someone behind for good is to desert them.

clue.text: No longer working, but unlikely to get a flat

explanation.surface: A pensioner is no longer at work and is in no rush to buy an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as RE-TIRED: a car fitted with new tyres (American spelling tires) is unlikely to get a puncture, a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensioners have stopped work for good; a vehicle given new tyres is less likely to suffer a puncture.

clue.text: Worm-catching communications satellite

explanation.surface: A satellite that relays messages is pictured as going after worms.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says the early bird catches the worm; Early Bird was also the nickname of Intelsat I, the first commercial communications satellite, launched in 1965.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb's prompt riser catches the worm, and Intelsat I bore the nickname as a broadcasting relay in orbit.

clue.text: Tailoring trade gets assessed for community charge

indicators.note: tailoring cuts and alters cloth, so the letters of trade are cut and reshaped

explanation.surface: A tailor's business is valued by the council for local tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailoring trade' reads as one phrase, a clothing business, but 'Tailoring' is the anagram signal working on 'trade'. The community charge was a British local tax, successor to the rates.
explanation.definitionFit: Property valued for local taxation was formerly said to be assessed for the rates.

clue.text: Day when alumni return to southern university

indicators.note: the graduates going back reads the letters of their abbreviation backwards

parts.note: alumni are graduates, holders of BA degrees, so BAs
Bath is a university city in the south-west of England

explanation.surface: Graduates go back to their old university on a particular day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns BAS into SAB. Bath is a university city in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekly holy day of rest is a particular day of the week.

clue.text: Some of Ursa Minor's debris returns to be seen from Earth by only a few

definitions.text: seen from Earth by only a few

indicators.note: returns says the picked letters come back the other way
Some says only part of the run of letters in the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: Fragments from the constellation Ursa Minor fall back to Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks OFU from 'of Ursa' and 'returns' turns it round. 'Minor's debris' finishes the surface only; a flying saucer is seen by few observers.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying saucers and similar unexplained objects are claimed as sightings by a small number of observers.

clue.text: Aquatints?

parts.note: aquatint is an etching technique, but split as aqua plus tints it reads as water plus colours

explanation.walkthrough: An aquatint is really a kind of print; the question mark licenses splitting it into Latin aqua, water, and tints.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings made with water-soluble pigments are literally water tints.

clue.text: Articles-a collection of literary anecdotes

parts.note: an is an indefinite article
a is the other indefinite article

explanation.surface: A heading for some pieces of writing introduces a gathering of literary stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A suffix-turned-noun for a miscellany of sayings and gossip about a writer.

clue.text: A popular little paper

parts.note: a popular newspaper printed on a smaller page size than a broadsheet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' seems to belittle the paper, but it refers to the smaller page format.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass-market newspapers are printed in a compact page format half the size of a broadsheet.

clue.text: Reprimand for not getting togged up

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for failing to dress smartly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Togged up' is British slang for dressed in one's best clothes; dressing down means dressing casually.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe scolding, and also choosing casual clothes over smart ones.

clue.text: See about the German left when getting on in years

indicators.note: about says the see goes round the other pieces

parts.note: Ely is a bishop's see, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A man notices that the German has gone, at his advanced age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts DERL inside ELY. A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is an English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: People advancing in age are old.

clue.text: A block which, understandably, is found under a shroud

definitions.text: A block which, understandably, is found under a shroud

parts.words: A block which, understandably, is found under a shroud
parts.note: on a sailing ship a shroud is a rope bracing the mast, and the round wooden block fixing it at the bottom bears a grim name fitting a corpse in a burial cloth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shroud' suggests a burial cloth, hence 'understandably' for something dead beneath it; at sea a shroud is a mast's rigging rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors give that name to the three-holed wooden block securing rigging to the hull.

clue.text: Dance around having been thrashed

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of dance are moved round into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone dances about after a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beaten with a stick as a punishment is a thrashing.

clue.text: Hides land destroyed by lazy workforce

indicators.note: destroyed says the letters of hides and land are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Animal skins and farmland are ruined by workers who cannot be bothered.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says the devil finds work for idle hands; 'hands' as workers makes a lazy workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands are workers, and idle ones are lazy staff.

clue.text: One prone to sermonising

parts.note: prone seems to mean inclined to, but it also means lying down, and a church helper who is not ordained may preach

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prone to' reads as 'inclined to'; taken literally, prone means lying flat, the pun on lay.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensed lay member of the Church of England may lead services and preach without being ordained.

clue.text: Gun Al produced in a lazy way-sluggishly

indicators.note: produced says the letters of Gun and Al are made into something new

parts.note: doing something in a lazy way is doing it idly

explanation.surface: A man called Al moves slowly and reluctantly, a gunslinger with no energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' turns GUN AL into LANGU.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving without energy or vigour is moving slowly and listlessly.

clue.text: People lifting their heads a lot? In bad golf you find it

definitions.text: People lifting their heads a lot?

indicators.note: bad says the letters of golf and you come out wrong and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A golfer keeps lifting their head, a fault found in poor play.
explanation.walkthrough: Lifting the head is a classic golfing fault, fitting the golf surface; in fact the people looking up are sky-watchers hunting flying saucers.
explanation.definitionFit: Studying unidentified flying objects means a lot of gazing at the sky.

clue.text: Hymn to a Greek deity each included

indicators.note: included says one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and the wild

explanation.surface: A song of praise to a Greek god, with everyone joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts EA inside PAN. 'to a' merely joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A song of praise or triumph, originally to Apollo.

clue.text: Remains within easy reach of Naples

definitions.text: Remains within easy reach of Naples

parts.words: Remains within easy reach of Naples
parts.note: remains looks like a verb, stays close by, but it is a noun: ruins of a Roman town near the Bay of Naples

explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' reads as a verb, stays; it is the noun, archaeological ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman town buried by Vesuvius in AD 79 survives as excavated ruins near the Campanian capital.

clue.text: Broken bone Len has to raise

indicators.note: broken says the letters of bone and Len are smashed and reset

explanation.surface: A man called Len has to set a fractured bone.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to elevate them to the peerage.

clue.text: Liberate one soul in torment

indicators.note: in torment says the letters of one and soul are twisted and tortured into a new order

explanation.surface: Freeing a single tormented spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: To unloose is to set free or release.

clue.text: Some slackness exposed by the cricket team

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A team's sloppy fielding is shown up.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'by' into the definition; it is a link word, and the team alone defines the answer. Essex is an English county with a first-class cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: Essex County Cricket Club plays first-class cricket in England.

clue.text: Dressed like a lord, while is missus went down the pit

parts.note: 'er indoors is slang for a man's wife, the missus, so 'er (her)
a miner going down the pit mined coal

explanation.surface: A peer in his robes, while his wife works down a coal mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is 'his' with the h dropped, matching 'er for her. Peers' ceremonial robes are trimmed with ermine fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers wear robes trimmed with white stoat fur on state occasions.

clue.text: They educate communities in the main

explanation.surface: Institutions that teach also serve communities in general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly' but means at sea: shoals of fish are groups in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Places of learning teach pupils; groups of fish swim together at sea.

clue.text: A lady's man by the year's end

parts.note: a man is he

indicators.note: end says the last letter of year's is taken

explanation.surface: A woman's husband arrives by the end of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun belonging to a woman.

clue.text: Window at the front of the ship?

explanation.surface: A window placed at the forward end of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: A bow window is a curved bay window.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved bay window takes its name from the forward part of a vessel's hull.

clue.text: Press up maybe for a military rehearsal

explanation.surface: Doing press-ups as part of practice for the forces.
explanation.walkthrough: Press-ups are a drill done by soldiers; the same phrase means a large-scale training manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers do press-ups in drill, and troops stage mock battles as training manoeuvres.
